results.label: Theorem 2.1 (Nonadaptive upper bound).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem1] Theorem 2.1 (Nonadaptive upper bound).
 [S2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$ , let  $r=\operatorname{rank}(A)$ , and let  $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ . There is a randomized algorithm such that the following holds for every fixed  $b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ . Its queried coordinates are fixed before any label is read and depend only on  $A$ ,  $\varepsilon$ , and private randomness. It queries at most
 [S2.E3] 
 $\min\left\{n,Cr\left(\log^{6}(2n)+\frac{\log^{4}(2n)}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\right\}$ (2.3)

distinct coordinates of  $b$  and, with probability at least  $0.99$  over its private randomness, returns  $\widehat{x}$  satisfying
 [S2.Ex1] 
 $F_{b}(\widehat{x})^{1/2}\leq(1+\varepsilon)\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}F_{b}(x)^{1/2}.$

results.label: Theorem 2.2 (Matching adaptive lower bound).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem2] Theorem 2.2 (Matching adaptive lower bound).
 [S2.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
There is an absolute constant  $c>0$  such that the following holds. For all integers  $n,d,r$  with  $1\leq r\leq\min\{n,d\}$  and every  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/800$ , there is a fixed matrix  $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$  of rank exactly  $r$  such that every adaptive randomized algorithm that, for every fixed  $b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ , returns  $\widehat{x}$  satisfying  $F_{b}(\widehat{x})^{1/2}\leq(1+\varepsilon)\min_{x}F_{b}(x)^{1/2}$  with probability at least  $0.99$  obeys
 [S2.E4] 
 $\sup_{b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{R}}Q(A,b)\geq c\min\left\{n,\frac{r}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right\}.$ (2.4)

Here  $Q$  may be a stopping-time query count and  $\mathcal{R}$  is the algorithm’s private seed. Specifically,  $Q$  counts distinct queried coordinates. Repeated requests are permitted but can be answered from the algorithm’s cache and are not charged twice; set  $Q=\infty$  on a run that never returns an output.

results.label: Corollary 2.3 (Minimax label complexity).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem3] Corollary 2.3 (Minimax label complexity).
 [S2.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Fix  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/800$  and  $1\leq r\leq\min\{n,d\}$ . Let  $\mathfrak{A}$  range over randomized algorithms that, for every fixed pair  $(A,b)$ , achieve the  $(1+\varepsilon)$ -approximation to  $F_{b}^{1/2}$  in (2.2) with probability at least  $0.99$ , and define
 [S2.E5] 
 $\mathcal{Q}_{n,d,r}(\varepsilon):=\inf_{\mathfrak{A}}\ \sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}:\,\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{R}}Q_{\mathfrak{A}}(A,b),$ (2.5)

where the expectation is over all algorithmic randomness. For absolute constants  $c,C>0$ ,
 [S2.EGx1] 
 $\displaystyle c\min\left\{n,\frac{r}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right\}$  $\displaystyle\leq\mathcal{Q}_{n,d,r}(\varepsilon)$ 

 $\displaystyle\leq\min\left\{n,Cr\left(\log^{6}(2n)+\frac{\log^{4}(2n)}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right)\right\}.$ (2.6)

The upper algorithm is nonadaptive, whereas the lower bound holds against adaptive algorithms. Thus the minimax label complexity is  $\widetilde{\Theta}(\min\{n,r/\varepsilon^{2}\})$ .

results.label: Lemma 3.1 (Huber triangle and increment inequalities).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 3.1 (Huber triangle and increment inequalities).
 [S3.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every  $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ ,
 [S3.EGx2] 
 $\displaystyle\psi_{H}(s+t)$  $\displaystyle\leq\psi_{H}(s)+\psi_{H}(t),$ (3.1)

 $\displaystyle\left\lvert\psi_{H}(s)-\psi_{H}(t)\right\rvert$  $\displaystyle\leq\psi_{H}(s-t),$ (3.2)

 $\displaystyle\left\lvert H(s)-H(t)\right\rvert$  $\displaystyle\leq\sqrt{H(s-t)}\bigl(\sqrt{H(s)}+\sqrt{H(t)}\bigr).$ (3.3)

Consequently, for nonnegative weights  $w_{i}$  and vectors  $y,z$  of the same finite dimension,
 [S3.E4] 
 $\left(\sum_{i}w_{i}H(y_{i}+z_{i})\right)^{1/2}\leq\left(\sum_{i}w_{i}H(y_{i})\right)^{1/2}+\left(\sum_{i}w_{i}H(z_{i})\right)^{1/2}.$ (3.4)

results.label: Lemma 3.2 (Imported multiscale covering primitive).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 3.2 (Imported multiscale covering primitive).
 [S3.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Fix  $\alpha\geq 1$ , and let  $\mathcal{I}\subset\mathbb{Z}$  be a finite contiguous interval with  $\left\lvert\mathcal{I}\right\rvert\geq 4\log(2N)$ . Suppose that  $\{w^{(j)}:j\in\mathcal{I}\}$  is an  $\alpha$ -approximate Huber weight scheme, meaning that for every  $i$  and  $j\in\mathcal{I}$ ,
 [S3.E8] 
 $\frac{2^{j}}{\alpha}\leq\frac{H(v_{i}(w^{(j)}))}{w_{i}^{(j)}v_{i}(w^{(j)})^{2}}\leq\alpha 2^{j},$ (3.8)

and  $w_{i}^{(j+1)}\leq\alpha w_{i}^{(j)}$  whenever  $j,j+1\in\mathcal{I}$ . Put
 [S3.E9] 
 $\lambda_{i}^{(j)}:=w_{i}^{(j)}v_{i}(w^{(j)})^{2},\qquad\tau_{i}^{\mathcal{I}}:=\max_{j\in\mathcal{I}}\lambda_{i}^{(j)},\qquad k_{\mathcal{I}}:=\max\mathcal{I}+1.$ (3.9)

Define the associated deterministic metric by
 [S3.E10] 
 $d_{\tau^{\mathcal{I}}}(h,k):=\max_{i\leq N}\sqrt{\frac{H(a_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}(h-k))}{\tau_{i}^{\mathcal{I}}}}.$ (3.10)

Then  $\sum_{i}\lambda_{i}^{(j)}=r$ , and for a constant  $C_{\alpha}$  depending only on  $\alpha$ ,
 [S3.E11] 
 $\gamma_{2}\!\left(K_{2^{k_{\mathcal{I}}}},d_{\tau^{\mathcal{I}}}\right)\leq C_{\alpha}2^{k_{\mathcal{I}}/2}\log^{3/2}(2N).$ (3.11)

There is a universal numerical  $\alpha_{0}$  for which such a scheme has a deterministic finite construction from  $(A,\mathcal{I})$  in the exact-real model.

results.label: Lemma 3.3 (Endpoint coverings).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 3.3 (Endpoint coverings).
 [S3.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
For  $p\in\{1,2\}$ , the scores in (3.14) have total mass  $r$ . With
 [S3.E15] 
 $d_{p}(h,k):=\max_{i\leq N}\frac{\left\lvert a_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}(h-k)\right\rvert^{p/2}}{\sqrt{\lambda_{i}^{(p)}}},$ (3.15)

they satisfy, for every  $S>0$ ,
 [S3.E16] 
 $\gamma_{2}\bigl(\{h:\left\lVert Ah\right\rVert_{p}^{p}\leq S\},d_{p}\bigr)\leq C\sqrt{S}\,\log^{3/2}(2N).$ (3.16)

results.label: Lemma 3.4 (All-radius label-oblivious Huber scores).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem4] Lemma 3.4 (All-radius label-oblivious Huber scores).
 [S3.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
There are scores  $\tau_{i}=\tau_{i}(A)>0$ , computable from  $A$  alone, such that
 [S3.E17] 
 $T:=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tau_{i}\leq Cr\log(2N)$ (3.17)

and, for
 [S3.E18] 
 $d_{\tau}(h,k):=\max_{i\leq N}\sqrt{\frac{H(a_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}(h-k))}{\tau_{i}}},$ (3.18)

one has, simultaneously for every  $R>0$ ,
 [S3.E19] 
 $\gamma_{2}(K_{R},d_{\tau})\leq C\sqrt{R}\,\log^{3/2}(2N).$ (3.19)

results.label: Lemma 3.5 (Unshifted expectation bound).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem5] Lemma 3.5 (Unshifted expectation bound).
 [S3.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
There is an absolute constant  $C$  such that, whenever
 [S3.E21] 
 $\alpha:=C\sqrt{\frac{T\log^{3}(2N)}{m}}\leq 1,$ (3.21)

then, for every  $R>0$ ,
 [S3.E22] 
 $\mathbb{E}\sup_{h\in K_{R}}\left\lvert\widehat{\Phi}(h)-\Phi(h)\right\rvert\leq 2\alpha R.$ (3.22)

In particular,
 [S3.E23] 
 $\mathbb{E}\sup_{h\in K_{R}}\widehat{\Phi}(h)\leq 3R.$ (3.23)

results.label: Lemma 3.6 (Centered affine transfer).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem6] Lemma 3.6 (Centered affine transfer).
 [S3.Thmtheorem6.p1] 
Fix  $B\geq 1$ ,  $0<\eta,\delta<1/2$ , and  $z$  with  $R=F_{z}(0)>0$ . There is a constant  $\overline{C}_{B}=O(B^{2})$ , depending only on  $B$ , such that if
 [S3.E26] 
 $m\geq\overline{C}_{B}\frac{T\log^{3}(2N)}{\eta^{2}\delta^{2}},$ (3.26)

then, with probability at least  $1-\delta$  over the fresh main sample,
 [S3.E27] 
 $\sup_{h\in K_{BR}}\left\lvert[\widehat{F}_{z}(h)-\widehat{F}_{z}(0)]-[F_{z}(h)-F_{z}(0)]\right\rvert\leq\eta R.$ (3.27)

The distribution depends on  $A$ , but not on  $z$ .

results.label: Remark 3.7 (Why centering matters).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem7] Remark 3.7 (Why centering matters).
 [S3.Thmtheorem7.p1] 
The conclusion is additive, localized, and centered. It does not claim that  $\widehat{F}_{z}$  multiplicatively preserves the full affine objective. An unseen residual may make the common baseline arbitrarily large, but it cannot destroy preservation of the increments needed for optimization.

results.label: Lemma 3.8 (Huber all-scale extension).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem8] Lemma 3.8 (Huber all-scale extension).
 [S3.Thmtheorem8.p1] 
Let  $N>16$ ,  $S_{0}:=8N^{3}$ , and  $\zeta:=1/16$ . Suppose
 [S3.E28] 
 $G(h):=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\omega_{i}H(a_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}h),\qquad\omega_{i}\geq 0,\qquad\sum_{i}\omega_{i}\leq 2N.$ (3.28)

If  $\left\lvert G(h)-\Phi(h)\right\rvert\leq\zeta\Phi(h)$  whenever  $\Phi(h)\in[1/2,S_{0}]$ , then
 [S3.E29] 
 $\left\lvert G(h)-\Phi(h)\right\rvert\leq 2\zeta\Phi(h)\qquad\text{for every }h.$ (3.29)

results.label: Lemma 3.9 (Label-oblivious constant-factor pilot).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem9] Lemma 3.9 (Label-oblivious constant-factor pilot).
 [S3.Thmtheorem9.p1] 
Fix  $b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$  and set  $F_{b}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{N}H(a_{i}^{\mathsf{T}}x-b_{i})$ . For independent  $\mu_{1},\ldots,\mu_{m_{0}}\sim\pi^{\rm pil}$ , define
 [S3.EGx5] 
 $\displaystyle\widetilde{\Phi}_{0}(h)$  $\displaystyle:=\frac{1}{m_{0}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_{0}}\frac{H(a_{\mu_{j}}^{\mathsf{T}}h)}{\pi_{\mu_{j}}^{\rm pil}},$ (3.33)

 $\displaystyle\widetilde{F}_{0}(x)$  $\displaystyle:=\frac{1}{m_{0}}\sum_{j=1}^{m_{0}}\frac{H(a_{\mu_{j}}^{\mathsf{T}}x-b_{\mu_{j}})}{\pi_{\mu_{j}}^{\rm pil}}.$ (3.34)

With probability at least  $1-\delta_{0}$ ,
 [S3.E35] 
 $(1-\rho)\Phi(h)\leq\widetilde{\Phi}_{0}(h)\leq(1+\rho)\Phi(h)\qquad\text{for every }h.$ (3.35)

Let  $x_{c}$  be the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm point in  $\arg\min\widetilde{F}_{0}$ , selected using only the pilot indices and labels, and let  $x_{*}\in\arg\min F_{b}$ ,  $F_{*}:=F_{b}(x_{*})$ . Except with total probability  $2\delta_{0}$ ,
 [S3.E36] 
 $R:=F_{b}(x_{c})\leq C_{0}F_{*},\qquad C_{0}:=\left(1+\frac{2}{\sqrt{(1-\rho)\delta_{0}}}\right)^{2}.$ (3.36)

results.label: Lemma 4.1 (Exact scalar majority gap).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 4.1 (Exact scalar majority gap).
 [S4.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $N\geq 1$  and  $0<\gamma\leq 1/2$ , and define
 [S4.E1] 
 $F_{\gamma}(t):=N(1/2-\gamma)H(4t)+N(1/2+\gamma)H(4(t-1)).$ (4.1)

Put
 [S4.E2] 
 $q_{\gamma}:=\frac{1/2-\gamma}{1/2+\gamma},\qquad t_{\gamma}^{*}:=1-\frac{q_{\gamma}}{4}.$ (4.2)

Then  $t_{\gamma}^{*}$  is a global minimizer, and every  $t\leq 1/2$  satisfies
 [S4.E3] 
 $F_{\gamma}(t)-F_{\gamma}(t_{\gamma}^{*})\geq 2\gamma N\frac{1+4\gamma}{1+2\gamma}\geq 2\gamma N.$ (4.3)

For a negative empirical majority, the symmetric statement holds with  $t\mapsto 1-t$ .

results.label: Lemma 4.2 (Binary rate–distortion).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 4.2 (Binary rate–distortion).
 [S4.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Let  $S$  be uniform on  $\{-1,+1\}^{r}$ , and let  $\widehat{S}$  be any  $\{-1,+1\}^{r}$ -valued estimate jointly distributed with  $S$ . If  $\mathbb{E}d_{H}(S,\widehat{S})<0.04r$ , then
 [S4.E5] 
 $\mathrm{I}(S;\widehat{S})\geq c_{\rm RD}r,\qquad c_{\rm RD}:=\log 2-h_{2}^{\rm nat}(0.04)>0.525.$ (4.5)

results.label: Lemma 4.3 (Finite adaptive-transcript bound).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 4.3 (Finite adaptive-transcript bound).
 [S4.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Let  $S$  be any random variable, let  $B=(B_{1},\ldots,B_{n})$  be a random response vector, and let  $\mathcal{R}$  be a private seed independent of  $(S,B)$ . Suppose an adaptive algorithm returns almost surely after  $Q$  fresh coordinate queries to  $B$ . For  $t=1,\ldots,n$ , let  $Z_{t}=\dagger$  if  $Q<t$ , and otherwise let  $Z_{t}=(J_{t},B_{J_{t}})$  record the  $t$ -th fresh index and response. Put  $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}:=\sigma(\mathcal{R},Z_{1},\ldots,Z_{t-1})$ . The active indicator and  $J_{t}$  on the active event are  $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$ -measurable. For an active history  $h$ , let  $I_{h}$  denote mutual information under the regular conditional law given  $h$ . If  $I_{h}(S;B_{J_{t}(h)})\leq\kappa$  for almost every active history, then
 [S4.E6] 
 $\mathrm{I}(S;\mathcal{R},Z_{1:n})\leq\kappa\,\mathbb{E}Q.$ (4.6)

results.label: Proposition 5.1 (Simple surrogate minimizers can be polynomially bad).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem1] Proposition 5.1 (Simple surrogate minimizers can be polynomially bad).
 [S5.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For all sufficiently large  $N$ , there are one-dimensional instances on which the exact least-squares minimizer has Huber-norm approximation ratio  $\Theta(N^{1/4})$ , and instances on which the exact  $\ell_{1}$ -regression minimizer has ratio  $\Theta(\sqrt{N})$ .
